target_customer: Restaurants, online ordering platforms and delivery fleets that need to dispatch orders to delivery providers
problem: Businesses that offer delivery have to build their own software to collect orders and dispatch drivers across multiple delivery services.
business_model: B2B SaaS and per-delivery fees on a delivery network and API

founders.name: Andrew Nakkache
previous_startups: Habitat Logistics (restaurant delivery; its delivery operations were sold in 2022 and the software became FIRST)
founders.background_notes: Education from the YC page bio.

founders.name: Michael Paszkiewicz
founders.background_notes: Listed as co-founder and CTO by the Ben Franklin Technology Partners page; also on the YC page.

competitors.name: Olo Dispatch
competitors.what: Dispatch product that pairs restaurant orders with third-party couriers such as Postmates and UberRUSH
competitors.traction_then: operating across most major markets per Olo

technical_complexity.rationale: Order aggregation, dispatch rules and integrations with many couriers and ordering systems is standard but integration heavy; the team had run it live on its own deliveries.

defensibility.rationale: Integrations and a courier network create some lock-in, but dispatch aggregation was offered by Olo and others and DoorDash Drive was available to restaurants.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Large players offered similar dispatch; FIRST sold its own delivery operations in January 2022 and kept the software, still operating per its site.

market_need_then: Restaurants were adding delivery fast in 2018 and 2019 and had to build software themselves; the founders say they delivered over 1 million orders on software they built.

branding.domain_note: Uses firstdelivery.com, not first.com; the company is also called First Delivery.

rebrands.why: Delivery operations were sold to Bring Me That and the company refocused on software; the reason for the new name is not stated

brand_strength.rationale: A generic one-word name that is hard to search; coverage is mostly directory entries and trade press interviews, with no sign the brand drove growth.

pivots.from: Running delivery operations for restaurants as Habitat Logistics plus software
pivots.to: Software only, with a delivery network and API
pivots.why: Sold delivery assets to Bring Me That and chose to double down on software, per CEO quote in the press release

outcome_analysis: FIRST grew out of a Philadelphia restaurant delivery business and became a delivery dispatch software company claiming 3M+ deliveries and 7K+ merchants. It sold its delivery operations in January 2022 and kept the software, which is still operating. Disclosed funding is tiny and unverified, so the scale of the business is unclear.
notes: Funding: only aggregators. One lists a $150K seed in March 2018 (startupintros) and CB Insights lists $500K total with investors including BringMeThat, Y Combinator and Avalanche VC; both unverified and conflicting, so no round is recorded. The Ben Franklin page says Habitat was backed in 2019 by investors who also backed DoorDash, Instacart and Caviar, without names or amounts. The exit is an asset sale of the delivery operations, not a sale of the company, so exit.type is none. Olo Dispatch source date is from the search summary (September 2015). YC page says founded 2014.
